title: How to Prepare for Carpet Installation: Furniture, Doors and Old Carpet
meta: Clear the small stuff, leave heavy furniture to the crew, plan for doors and old carpet removal. Wills Flooring's carpet prep checklist for Everett homes.
keywords: how to prepare for carpet installation, what to do before carpet installers come, do carpet installers move furniture, remove old carpet before installation, carpet installation checklist, doors after new carpet

blocks.lead: Empty the closets and small items, leave the heavy furniture to the crew if it is in the quote, do not pull the old carpet yourself unless you have agreed to, and expect interior doors to come off for the day.
blocks.detail: Most Everett carpet jobs are one day per floor. The prep that matters happens the week before: deciding who moves what, who removes the old carpet, and what happens to doors that will not clear the new pile.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks, "Installers are coming Tuesday, what do I actually need to do?" The answer depends on what your quote says, and Everett has every version of the job: a Silver Lake two-story where a Boeing shift worker needs the bedrooms done while the house is empty, a Riverside 1910s home with original doors and uneven floors, and a Port Gardner condo with an elevator to reserve. This is the carpet installation checklist we send our own customers, in the order things need to happen.

blocks.text: Furniture: what to move and what to leave

items.title: You handle the small stuff
items.text: Everything on the floor that fits in a box: shoes, toys, baskets, floor lamps, cords, plants and the contents of closets. Anything on a low shelf that could fall when the wall shakes. Empty dressers of heavy contents if we are moving them; a full dresser is a two-person injury.

items.title: The crew handles the big pieces, if quoted
items.text: Beds, dressers, sofas and dining sets move from room to room as we work, then go back at the end. In a bedroom-only job they shift to the hallway or a finished room. Whole-house jobs need a staging plan, usually the garage or the kitchen, which is why we ask at the estimate.

items.title: What no installer moves
items.text: Pianos, gun safes, aquariums, waterbeds, pool tables and most large electronics. Those need a specialty mover or your own arrangements before the day. A grand piano in a Bayside living room has stopped more than one install at 8 a.m.

items.title: Timing for shift workers
items.text: Everett has a lot of Boeing and hospital schedules. If you sleep days, tell us, and we sequence rooms so the bedroom is done first or last. The crew arrives around 8 and a typical main floor is finished by mid afternoon.

blocks.title: Scope Your Carpet Project
blocks.sub: Tell us the rooms, the stairs and whether we are moving furniture and removing old carpet. We bring samples and a firm price to your door.

blocks.text: Old carpet: pull it yourself or leave it?

a.title: Choose this when
items: You want one day of disruption instead of a weekend of your own labor
There may be pet stains, mold or an unknown subfloor underneath
The house has stairs; tack strip on stairs is sharp and awkward
You want disposal handled; Everett transfer station runs cost time and a truck

b.title: Choose this when
items: The quote gives you a real credit for it, and you have asked
You are curious what is under it and want to look before the day
You can pull every staple and the tack strip without gouging the subfloor
You can leave the subfloor swept and clean, with nails and debris gone

blocks.title: If you find hardwood under the carpet:
blocks.text: Stop and call before the install date. Riverside and Bayside homes from the 1900s to 1920s often have fir or oak under the carpet. You may still want carpet, but you should decide with the wood in view, and the tack strip plan changes so the wood stays refinishable.

items.html: Interior doors come off. We take them down to work and rehang them at the end. If a thicker pad or a taller pile means a door drags, we tell you. Trimming the bottom of a door is a carpenter's task, not a carpet installer's, and hollow-core doors can only lose so much.
Baseboards stay. Carpet is tucked under the baseboard gap. Baseboards set tight to the subfloor in older Everett homes may show a small gap after; a bead of caulk fixes it.
Paint first, then carpet. Paint walls and trim before install day so drips land on old carpet. Touch-ups go on after we leave. Do not schedule a painter for the same day.
Heat on, windows openable. Carpet and pad relax and stretch better at room temperature. New carpet has a smell for a day or two; a window cracked open handles it.

items.text: We confirm the rooms, the carpet and pad, where furniture is going and where we can park the van. In a Port Gardner condo this is when the elevator pad and the quiet-hour window matter.

Old carpet is cut into strips, rolled and hauled with the pad. Staples and tack strip come out, the subfloor is swept and checked for squeaks, soft spots and stains. Anything unexpected gets shown to you before we cover it.
New tack strip around the perimeter, pad rolled, seamed and fastened. This is the loud part of the day.
Carpet is rough cut, seamed with a heat iron, then power stretched wall to wall and hooked onto the strip. Edges are tucked, doorways get their transitions, and doors go back on.

items.d: End of day · Furniture back and walkthrough
items.text: Furniture returns, scraps are yours if you want a piece for repairs, and we walk the rooms with you. Vacuuming right away is fine and helps pull up loose fibers from the cut edges.

items: Pets. Carpet day is loud and doors are open. A closed room with a blanket or a day at a friend's house is kinder for everyone.
Parking. In Riverside and near downtown Everett, street parking near the door saves the crew a lot of carrying.
The closet floor under a shelving system. Built-in closet systems bolted to the floor need to come out or be planned around.
Where the leftover carpet goes. Keep a piece the size of a doormat for future repairs; it will match perfectly in a way a new order will not.

faq.a: Most do when it is agreed in advance, and Wills Flooring lists it as a line on the written quote. Beds, dressers, sofas and tables are moved room to room and put back. Pianos, safes, aquariums, waterbeds and large electronics are never moved by the crew and need your own arrangements before the day.

faq.q: Should I remove the old carpet myself before installation?
faq.a: Only if you have asked for it and the quote reflects it. Our quotes include tear-out and disposal, so pulling it yourself rarely saves much and you lose the chance for us to see the subfloor first. If you do it, pull every staple and the tack strip, and sweep the floor clean.

faq.q: Do I need to take the doors off for carpet installation?
faq.a: No, the crew does that. Interior doors come off so the carpet can be tucked and stretched cleanly, then they are rehung. If the new pad and carpet are thicker than the old, a door may drag. We flag it before we leave; trimming a door is a carpenter's job.

faq.q: How long does carpet installation take in one day?
faq.a: A typical Everett main floor or three bedrooms is one working day, arriving around 8 and finishing mid afternoon, including tear-out. Stairs add several hours. Whole-house jobs with two floors and stairs run two days. Seams and stretching take the same care regardless of the size of the room.

faq.q: Should I paint before or after new carpet?
faq.a: Before. Paint walls and trim ahead of install day so drips land on the old carpet, then do small touch-ups afterward. Baseboards stay in place during carpet installation, so there is no need to wait for them. Never schedule a painter for the same day as the flooring crew.

faq.q: Can I vacuum new carpet right away?
faq.a: Yes. Vacuuming on day one is fine and helps lift loose fibers left from cutting the edges and seams. Shedding for the first few weeks is normal on cut-pile carpet and is not a defect. Use a vacuum with an adjustable height setting so the beater bar does not fuzz the pile.
